edits.text: - Keep a sentence‑initial single function word (determiner, pronoun, subordinating word, or auxiliary) attached to the following token so the resulting piece contains a lexical noun or main predicate.

- Keep a lone preposition or particle together with the immediately following phrase that supplies its object or complement; if a cut would leave the preposition/particle as a one-word piece, attach it to the next word so the piece contains the preposition/particle plus its noun-phrase or clause complement.

- Fallback: prefer a cut that includes the sentence-initial token together with the next content word (a lexical noun or main verb) over any cut that would leave a single sentence-initial function word alone.

- Fallback: prefer a cut that keeps a preposition or particle with its immediately following noun phrase or clause (i.e. place the cut after that complement) over a cut placed immediately after the preposition/particle; likewise prefer a cut that includes a sentence‑initial determiner/pronoun/subordinator/auxiliary with the following content word over a cut that would leave that single function word isolated.
